subject.title: Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages

question: Which restart message-recovery design should be canonical for this issue: the SQLite followup queue PR, a narrower drain-only mitigation, or a broader gateway restart/session recovery design?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the permanent fix touches persisted runtime state, replay ordering, channel delivery semantics, and multiple overlapping open PRs, so automation should not choose the product boundary alone.

options.title: Advance SQLite Queue Recovery
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 as the canonical candidate, resolve conflicts/proof/merge-risk issues, and close older partial PRs after that decision.

options.title: Narrow To Drain Mitigation
options.body: Prioritize a smaller pre-shutdown drain path such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/46303 and leave durable replay for a separate explicit design.

options.title: Pause For Broader Recovery Design
options.body: Keep this issue open under a wider gateway restart/session recovery plan before accepting new runtime storage or channel replay behavior.

recommendation.title: Advance SQLite Queue Recovery
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 as the canonical candidate, resolve conflicts/proof/merge-risk issues, and close older partial PRs after that decision.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent restart-drain work is the clearest current-main owner signal for choosing the gateway lifecycle boundary.
